newsitem.title: UK: POLL - Gilt/Bund spread to narrow for next two years.
newsitem.headline: POLL - Gilt/Bund spread to narrow for next two years.

text.p: The differential between British gilt and German Bund yields is expected to narrow over the next two years as interest rates peak and growth slows, a Reuters survey showed on Monday.
By end-1997, the spread between the 10-year gilt and Bund yields is expected to fall to 140 basis points, the median of 13 forecasts in the survey showed.
The median of seven forecasts for the gilt/Bund spread by mid-1999 was 80 basis points, compared to 165 on July 9, the final day of the survey.
Twenty-nine banks, investment and research houses provided forecasts for the quarterly survey of UK economic indicators, foreign exchange and interest rates.
Analysts said the bond yield cycles in Britain and Germany were not synchronised.

"As the British economy slows, demand for funds, investment or consumption in the UK will ease. This will allow long-term interest rates to fall," said Stephen Lewis, chief economist at London Bond Broking.

Ten-year gilt yields are expected to peak at 7.50 percent in the first half of 1998, the survey showed. From there, the median of predictions show yields falling to 6.90 percent by mid-1999 from current levels around 7.10 percent.
Forecasts for Britain's gross domestic product(GDP) produced a median of 3.4 percent year-on-year growth in the final quarter of this year.
The first quarter of 1999 will see GDP growth at 1.9 percent on the year, the survey showed. These compare to year-on-year GDP growth in the first quarter of 1997 at 3.10 percent.
Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown, in his budget announcement on July 2, forecast average GDP at 3.25 percent in 1997 and at 2.5 percent in 1998.
Analysts say a pick-up in domestic German demand will accelerate the recovery, which until now has been export-led. This will eventually translate into a narrowing spread.
"We feel the Bundesbank will probably return to a variable repo towards the end of this year. From there we will see German interest rates creeping up," said an analyst at Sakura Finance.
"Bund yields will then rapidly deteriorate, narrowing the differential."

The Bundesbank has been using a system of fixed repo rates, set at three percent since August 1996. But a variable rate will allow the market to have a say in interest rate levels via the bidding process.

Growing perceptions that Britain's new Labour government will aim to join European economic and monetary union (EMU) in 2001 is another reason for the predicted narrowing of the gilt/Bund spread, analysts said.
Nick Stamenkovic, economist at DKB International, made the lowest forecast at 20 basis points for the 10-year gilt/Bund spread by mid-1999.
"It will be the last EMU convergence play. At the moment domestic factors are affecting gilt yields," he said."Once interest rates have peaked, markets will start looking at policies."

Base rate forecasts in the survey showed a peak at seven or 7.25 percent in the first half of 1998. From there a gradual drop to 6.50 percent by mid-1999 is expected, a median of 15 predictions showed. Base rates were raised to 6.75 percent from 6.5 percent on Thursday, the day after the survey closed.
